title: Predicate-mapping registry — canonical vocabulary ⇄ bridged-project relations
description: The machine-validated bridge contract between pinakes's canonical node/edge vocabulary and the relation vocabularies of the projects it bridges (Analyzer, and — when insimul-bridge lands — Insimul). ONE registry, versioned on `registryVersion`; the authoritative copy is intended to live in Rosetta (~/Development/rosetta/registry/predicate-mapping.json) once that workspace exists, with this `shared/` copy kept in sync and never forked locally. Encodes the media-bridge mapping spec Appendix A: the Analyzer relation vocabulary, the sha256:/cs: id-space rules, the `local-only` portability class that keeps personal-tier facts from ever leaving the machine, and the t_start/t_end ⇄ time_start/time_end temporal-field map. Each relation entry names a canonical node/edge type (validated against shared/canonical-schema.json for totality) or a non-type mapping (derived rule / provenance columns / temporal fields); a `pending` flag marks types that are declared-but-not-yet-added canonical schema additions (e.g. the v1.3 `asset` node + `depicts`/`mentions` edges landed by analyzer-bridge US-003), so the flag doubles as a live checklist the totality test enforces against the evolving schema.

portabilityClasses.horn-safe: Crosses the boundary into pinakes's constrained-Horn Datalog layer (+ arithmetic after Phase 1).
portabilityClasses.grounding-only: Reference data consumed at ground time; no runtime predicate crosses.
portabilityClasses.full-prolog: Full ISO Prolog only (cuts / negation / probabilistic likelihood) — does not cross to Datalog.
portabilityClasses.local-only: Never leaves the personal tier. Hard-gated out of open-data releases, packaged corpora, and any non-personal export or training set (the privacy invariant this bridge introduces).

idSpaces.description: A content-addressed Analyzer asset (id = sha256 of bytes) → canonical `asset` node. Re-encode changes the hash; `derived-from` lineage partially compensates (registry future-work).
A grounded canonical pinakes entity (csid). The Bridge-1 `refers_to` target: a fact may reference a real-world entity, not only an asset hash.
An Analyzer run. Default: fact provenance only, not a graph node.
A versioned Analyzer EDL take. Default: fact provenance only, not a graph node.

analyzer.title: Analyzer — agentic multimedia studio (the user's file web)
analyzer.sourceDoc: the media-bridge mapping spec Appendix A

direction.AR->LS: Analyzer predicate → pinakes canonical (Bridge 2: the file web as corpus).
direction.LS->AR: pinakes canonical → Analyzer (Bridge 1: entity grounding + world knowledge).

pendingSchemaAdditions.note: Landed by analyzer-bridge US-003 (may already be present from the Insimul v1.2 bump). Flip the relation `pending` flags to false when these types resolve in shared/canonical-schema.json.

relations.notes: container / duration / codec / width / height sub-facts → asset node properties, not edges.
Vision caption / detected object. Object X may carry an entity_ref (csid) after Bridge-1 grounding.
ASR segments → asset transcript property + temporal facts; t_start/t_end ⇄ time_start/time_end (see temporalFieldMap).
Article / text ingest → asset text property.
Temporal segmentation facts; endpoints map through temporalFieldMap.
A derived rule, never a stored edge — same derived-not-stored discipline as pinakes's temporal edges.
Existing canonical edge type. Lineage transitivity is one Horn rule (US-004).
Bridge-1 grounding: `depicts`/`mentions` with entity_ref = csid. Confidence from the grounding rubric; ambiguous candidates never auto-merged.
US-CS6 constraint facts → rules-registry entries + violation facts. Third instance of the provenanced-rules pattern (pinakes Phase 4b, Insimul validators).
Canonical nodes (culture / place / language / deity / …) exported as the shared GroundingPack format (same schema as the Insimul bridge).

relations.external: fact provenance {source, source_url, retrieved_at, confidence, license}
relations.notes: The US-PL1 alignment — identical field names. `license` is an SPDX id; facts derived from licensed reference data keep the license through the bridge.
